facts.fact: The CDC Foundation case study says deaths are notified and captured within INRIS, Zambia's civil registration system, with death registration coverage risen from under 4 per cent to 42 per cent; the body prints no date and the published year is used.

The CDC Foundation case study says the expansion of INRIS has brought access to CRVS services to 81 of 116 districts, covering 83 per cent of the population; it does not count offices registering, and prints no date, so the published year is used.

The case study names the Department of National Registration, Passport and Citizenship as the body running death registration and INRIS, jointly with the Ministry of Health for e-death notification; undated, published year used.

The case study says UNICEF and Bloomberg Philanthropies supported the expansion of INRIS, and that partners including the Data for Health Initiative are equipping INRIS kits in select district registration offices and hospital mortuaries; no domestic budget line is stated; undated, published year used.
